texts: good. the winter, its 'bad' description, the coming and the 112-year gap back from now are all recorded and queryable.
good. the two wraiths are counted as a group of two and each wraith also gets its own emergence, with the bad-winter frame and the 112-year gap carried on both.

mixed: everything the sentence says is recorded (the harvest, its salt-bloom kind, the failure, the 112-year gap), but the translator also emitted a stray taxonomy claim that a salt-bloom is a bloom, for a symbol nothing else in the parse uses. Nothing in your wording caused that, so the sentence needs no change; if you do want salt-bloom itself to become a queryable kind, give it its own head: 'The harvest of salt-bloom failed one hundred and twelve years ago.'
good. the spring tide, the wrong moon phase as the time of the coming, and the 112-year gap are all present, with both compounds linked to their plain kinds.
good. the rationing, the Council as its agent, the mire-essence, and the ordering after the 112-year-old bad winter are all recorded.

good. 'very' is kept as a degree on 'bad' beside the plain 'bad', and the 63-year gap is anchored on now. One thing to watch across this item: this sentence and 'The spring tide came...' file the subject of 'came' in one participant slot while 'A bad winter came one hundred and twelve years ago.' and 'A bad winter came twenty-six years ago.' file it in another, so a single query for what 'came' will not return all four.
good. four wraiths are counted as a group, each wraith also gets its own emergence, and the Sunken Cove is recorded as the source with both its name and its kind.
good. being a boy is anchored as a past state sixty-three years ago and also kept as a plain past fact about Old Vesh, and the whole capitalized name is one symbol.

bad: the person symbol here is built from 'Vesh' alone while the two neighbouring sentences build it from the whole name 'Old Vesh', so the father is hung on a second, separate individual and will not link to the Old Vesh of those sentences. The wording itself is fine and the slip is on the translator's side; if you want to remove the risk entirely, use one unvarying form of the name everywhere in the item — 'Vesh's father was a Keeper sixty-three years ago.' with plain 'Vesh' throughout.

bad: 'three other Keepers' makes the translator infer, and then assert outright, that the father was himself a Keeper — a claim no word in the sentence makes — while the exclusion carried by 'other' is dropped anyway, so you pay for an invented fact and get nothing for it. State his membership in words and drop 'other': 'Sixty-three years ago, Old Vesh's father, a Keeper himself, walked the Cove Stair every evening with three Keepers.'
good. the Council, the creating, the modern feather-ration system with its plain 'system' link, and the 63-year gap are all recorded.
good. same clean shape as the other 'a bad winter came' sentences, with the 26-year gap anchored on now.

mixed: everything is recorded except the count — a numeral on a singular subject has no slot to ride on, so 'one' is silently dropped, while 'two wraiths' and 'four wraiths' elsewhere in this item do keep their counts and stay countable. If the tally matters, put the singleness in a word that can be stored as a property of the wraith: 'Twenty-six years ago, a lone wraith emerged.'

good. the ground feathers form a group with 'ground' passed down to each feather, the Stilllight Lantern keeps its name and kind, its 'around' position is kept as written, and 'warded back' is kept whole as one action.

good. the doubling, the Council, the Stilllight-linked feather ration and the 26-year gap are all recorded. Note only that 'for winter' was read as part of what the ration is (the winter ration) rather than as the occasion for doubling it; that is the likelier reading, but the sentence does not settle it.
